title: Implement modular quality metric adapters for quantization calibration
creator: Amit Shah
description: Goal: Build a modular, performance-sensitive metric adapter layer to plug into the quantization calibration and validation pipelines. The adapter layer will normalize outputs from model checkpoints (FP32/FP16/FP8/INT8 variants) and produce comparable quality signals across tasks: language modeling (perplexity), knowledge probes (MMLU-style accuracy), summarization (ROUGE variants, BERTScore), machine translation (BLEU), extractive QA (EM/F1), code generation (pass@k / compile+unit tests), and instruction-following heuristics. The adapter must be extensible so new task scorers can be added without pipeline changes, and efficient so metric computation does not dominate calibration runs. This ticket focuses on implementation of the adapter API, a couple of canonical scorer plugins, and integration hooks for the calibration orchestrator and the eval dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter API documented and implemented with versioned contract (input artifacts, refs, outputs) and unit tests
Perplexity adapter implemented and validated against FP32 baseline on wiki-text subset; results within expected variance thresholds
MMLU-style accuracy scorer implemented with expected scoring script and dataset split; can compare across precision variants
ROUGE and BLEU adapters added via plugin using existing eval libs; results stored in calibration results schema
End-to-end pipeline runs (quant calibration job) can attach metric outputs to the calibration artifact and surface them to the eval dashboard
Metric computation time accounted for in pipeline SLAs; adapters support sampling strategies to limit compute (configurable)
test_plan: Unit tests for adapter input validation, error handling, and metric normalization
Small-scale calibration runs (smoke) with FP32->FP8/INT8 model variants on 1K samples per task to verify outputs
Regression tests: run FP32 baseline and INT8 quantized run and assert known deltas for MMLU and perplexity on canonical subsets
Performance test: measure metric compute latency and GPU/CPU utilization; ensure metric step <20% of total calibration runtime for default sampling
Integration test: PR to calibration orchestrator that wires adapters and uploads results to the eval dashboard; verify dashboard ingestion
rollout_plan: Feature branch with adapters and two scorer plugins (perplexity, MMLU) — internal review
Merge to staging; run overnight calibration bundles on staging infra for 3 models across A100/GR4 instances
Add additional plugins (ROUGE, BLEU) in follow-up PR; validate storage schema compatibility
Deploy adapters to production calibration pipeline behind feature flag; enable for 10% of internal calibrations
Monitor metrics ingestion, compute cost, and signal quality; iterate on sampling and caching if needed
Full rollout after one-week stability and QA sign-off
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Metric computation time increases end-to-end calibration latency — Mitigation: implement sampling, async metric computation, and caching of repeated prefixes

Risk: Metric implementations produce non-comparable scores across precisions due to tokenization or generation differences — Mitigation: enforce shared tokenization, canonical decoding parameters, and provide normalization layer in adapter
Risk: Storage blowup from verbose metric artifacts — Mitigation: compress and summarize outputs (store scalars and sampled examples only), configurable retention
Risk: New scorer dependencies conflict with runtime environment — Mitigation: isolate scorer plugins in lightweight containers or use pinned wheels and dependency vetting
